nodes.label:
Neonate with suspected or confirmed
alloimmune haemolysis

DAT-NEGATIVE ABO disease:
NO DIRECT EVIDENCE identified
for IVIG. Individual clinical
judgement only.

Kell / anti-c / anti-E / mixed:
NO comparative evidence
(case reports only). Mechanistically
poor fit for IVIG in Kell disease —
consider EPO / iron / transfusion.

Rh-D or ABO confirmed.
Intensive (multi-light, continuous)
phototherapy already optimised?

Optimise intensive
phototherapy first —
re-assess bilirubin trend

Bilirubin still rising >8.5
micromol/L/hr, OR approaching the
exchange-transfusion threshold,
despite intensive phototherapy?

Continue intensive phototherapy
+ routine monitoring.
No IVIG indicated.

Is exchange transfusion
indicated AND immediately
available now?

PROCEED TO EXCHANGE
TRANSFUSION.
IVIG must NOT delay this.

Exchange delayed or unavailable:
IVIG may be considered as a
BRIDGING measure — 0.5–1 g/kg
single dose (may repeat once at 12h)

CAUTION — RCT evidence: GRADE Low–Moderate
certainty of NO benefit (Rh); Very low certainty
(ABO). Monitor for NEC 24–48h post-dose;
check FBC/DAT pre- and post-dose.

notes.text: Source: IVIG-HDFN evidence synthesis, Sep 2026 (systematised narrative review). See unit guideline for full thresholds, dosing and monitoring detail. IVIG must never delay a clinically indicated exchange transfusion.
